claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a homogenized high-temperature BCC alloy.
Phase stability in this alloy is governed jointly by the thermodynamic drive for chemical ordering and kinetic limitations on atomic diffusion.
The thermodynamic drive for chemical ordering is primarily induced by Al.
At lower temperatures, the composition makes the BCC structure thermodynamically unstable relative to ordered or phase-separated states.
Rapid cooling suppresses the atomic rearrangements needed for ordering or phase separation.
Suppressing atomic rearrangements by rapid cooling preserves a metastable BCC phase.
Slow cooling or isothermal holding at an intermediate temperature permits diffusion-mediated ordering and phase separation.
The relevant structural mediator is atomic-scale chemical ordering toward B2 or a related ordered phase.
Al alters nearest-neighbor interactions and thereby increases the local ordering tendency.
Atomic diffusivity during rapid cooling is too slow for the proposed ordering to evolve.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain the metastable BCC structure.
Slow-cooled or isothermally held samples will develop chemical ordering or phase separation, potentially including B2 or another secondary phase.
The rapidly quenched sample is designated as the homogeneous BCC baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies only in a processing window where cooling-rate-dependent kinetic constraints compete with the thermodynamic ordering drive.
Significant composition changes or the addition of other elements may cause deviations from the proposed mechanism.
The critical cooling rates and the identity of the ordered structure are not yet specified.

The hypothesis is designated as falsified if slow-cooled or isothermally held samples show no detectable ordering or secondary-phase differences from the quenched baseline, or if quenched samples show comparable ordering.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that processing is identical except for cooling rate, but the proposed comparison also introduces isothermal holds, which change hold duration and thermal history in addition to cooling rate.
